Across 11 datasets (n=478), MONS captured anger and disgust but was dissociable from general negative affect and affective arousal. Notably, MONS did not predict perceived moral wrongness in conventional moral judgment paradigms, suggesting that moral outrage is not reducible to more cognitive moral evaluation. Findings provide a moral outrage neurofunctional model that delineates its relationship to other affective states and distinguishes it from traditional moral judgment.

items.title: Sex-dependent gating of astrocyte-driven nociceptive plasticity
items.blurb: Sex differences in pain are well established, yet how nociceptive processing is differentially regulated across sexes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that spinal astrocytes provide pathway-specific control of acute nociceptive synaptic plasticity in rats. Chemogenetic activation of distinct astrocytic G-protein-coupled receptor pathways induced synaptic depression or potentiation at spinal nociceptive synapses in males, but failed to evoke detectable plasticity in females. Despite this lack of astrocyte-induced synaptic plasticity, females developed mechanical hypersensitivity comparable to males, revealing a dissociation between synaptic plasticity and pain-related behavior. Gonadectomy prevented astrocyte-induced plasticity in males, whereas testosterone treatment enabled Gq-dependent synaptic depression in ovariectomized females. Females exhibited more prominent perineuronal net labeling, and enzymatic degradation of extracellular matrix (ECM) components enabled Gq-dependent synaptic depression in females. Together, these findings identify hormonal status and ECM organization as important determinants of the susceptibility of spinal nociceptive circuits to astrocyte-driven synaptic plasticity.

items.title: Surrogate Verifiers Shape Decisions in Closed-Loop Experimental Design
items.blurb: High throughput, automated screening has revolutionized biological experimentation and prompted predictions of AI-enabled "self-driving" labs. Deployed autonomous lab systems typically use a learned surrogate to predict new experimental candidates and rank which conditions deserve expensive follow-up. Determining whether a computational surrogate verifier can substitute for an experimental assay's ground truth requires an understanding of model accuracy, uncertainty, and extrapolation. In this work, we present surrogate verifiers trained on N=7,688 Lacticaseibacillus growth curves exploring a 10-dimensional media component experimental design space. We train surrogate models across six distinct families including polynomial, Gaussian-process, tree-ensemble, neural, and Monod-kinetic forms to predict maximum optical density (OD600). Surrogates ranked by the most commonly reported accuracy metrics (held-out R^2; MAE; RMSE) disagree sharply on which experiments to test next and the best achievable yield. We evaluate models in a Bayesian optimization loop and find that the model used as the active learning oracle matters more than the acquisition function or batch size. We apply conformal calibration to build a model-agnostic assessment criterion of uncertainty and model coverage. We end by evaluating model accuracy and calibration under transfer to an unseen related bacterial strain, and confirm on a prospective validation plate that the transferred verifier's intervals fail in the direction and region our retrospective analysis predicts. This work explores the surrogate verifier within the loop as a previously underexplored axis of closed-loop design and points towards best calibration practices.

items.title: Universal barcoded connectomics for massively parallel single-neuron projection mapping in diverse vertebrate species
items.blurb: Neuroscience relies on diverse model species to understand animal behavior and brain function. Yet, tools for rapid, high-resolution brain connectivity mapping remain unavailable in most vertebrate species, slowing progress in many neuroscience models and rendering cross-species circuit comparisons challenging. Here, we overcome this barrier by establishing sequencing-based barcoded connectomics for rapid single-neuron tracing in seven vertebrate species ranging from frogs to birds to non-human primates. We develop a general solution to viral tropism and barcode trafficking, validate our reagents by mapping the projections of thousands of neurons in the songbird HVC, and discover a single set of reagents that functions across highly divergent species. Together, we provide ready-to-use barcoding reagents for diverse species and a simple framework for further adapting them if necessary, enabling high throughput single-neuron tracing across vertebrates.

items.title: Evolutionarily conserved coupling of lysosomal response sensing and disease-associated microglial reprogramming scales with pathological timescales
items.blurb: Background Microglia transition into disease-associated microglia (DAM) during central nervous system (CNS) injury and neurodegeneration, yet the upstream intracellular logic driving this state conversion in vivo remains unclear. The lysosome acts as a signaling hub, but whether physiological phagocytic load universally initiates and quantitatively couples to DAM reprogramming across different pathological timescales is unknown. Methods We established a rigorous, unit-corrected analytical framework to overcome pseudo-replication in public single-cell data, anchoring statistical inferences at the level of independent biological units (animals, sequencing plates, or donors). We integrated six transcriptomic datasets spanning three murine injury/amyloidosis models and three large-scale human neurodegenerative cohorts (>320,000 microglial nuclei), alongside human Alzheimer's disease (AD) GWAS summary statistics. Results We demonstrate that the MiT/TFE-regulated lysosomal biogenesis program temporally precedes DAM reprogramming and maintains an evolutionarily conserved baseline coupling even in uninjured homeostatic tissue. In human microglia, MITF and TFE3 transcripts closely track DAM activation, whereas post-translationally regulated TFEB mRNA does not. Genetic enrichment analysis (MAGMA) reveals that common AD risk does not act upon the upstream lysosomal program, but is strongly anchored downstream at APOE. Furthermore, Trem2-knockout models demonstrate that disease-induced coupling amplification retains roughly half its magnitude even when the mature DAM subpopulation collapses. Cross-system comparisons reveal a state-transition synchrony model: disease-driven amplification of lysosomal-DAM coupling ({Delta}) scales with pathological timescales, showing strong amplification in acute murine injury and aggressive amyloidosis (5xFAD {Delta} = +0.252), but manifesting primarily as steady baseline maintenance across decades-long asynchronous human AD progression (SEA-AD {Delta} = +0.072). Conclusions Our study establishes the lysosomal stress-DAM coupling as an evolutionarily conserved pacemaking module for microglial state transitions, providing a quantitative framework for therapeutically targeting neuroinflammation and tissue repair.

items.title: Neonatal exposure to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in mice is associated with localized changes in cerebral cortex cell proliferation
items.blurb: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can cause acute and persistent neurological manifestations, and evidence suggests these effects may be at least partly explained by direct effects of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein, which includes neuroinflammation, cognitive dysfunction, and persistent pain. Because the developing brain undergoes finely regulated processes of cellular proliferation, differentiation, and cerebrovascular maturation, exposure to SARS-CoV-2 or its components during this critical period may interfere with neurodevelopment. We therefore investigated whether neonatal exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein affects processes underlying brain development. To this end, we used a mouse model previously developed by our group, where Swiss mice received an injection (s.c.) of spike protein from the ancestral viral strain or vehicle at postnatal day 1 (P1). Body weight, body length, and the righting reflex were evaluated until postnatal day 20 (P20). At P10, mouse brains were analyzed for cell proliferation, neural cell populations, and cerebrovascular organization, while blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed at P20 using Evans Blue. Neonatal spike protein exposure did not affect body weight, body length, or postural righting reflex. At P10, cell proliferation in spike-exposed animals was comparable to control groups, whereas region-specific alterations in SOX2-positive cells and TBR1-positive neurons were observed. Spike protein exposure did not broadly alter cerebrovascular architecture or BBB permeability, although increased IB4 fluorescence was detected in the lateral dentate gyrus (DG). Our findings provide evidence that exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein during postnatal development can influence specific aspects of neural development, highlighting the importance of understanding how viral components may affect the developing brain during critical windows of vulnerability. Keywords: spike protein, brain development, coronavirus, COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2, cerebrovasculature.

items.title: Shox2 maintains thalamocortical neuron firing for whisker-based somatomotor responses and sleep spindles in mice
items.blurb: In the mouse thalamus, thalamocortical neurons (TCNs) relay sensory information to cortex and generate rhythmic activity, including sleep spindles, through precisely timed firing. TCNs switch between tonic and burst firing modes that depend on intrinsic membrane properties, yet what maintains these properties in the mature thalamus remains unknown. Transcription factors, which regulate the ion channel genes that shape firing, are natural candidates. Here, we investigate Shox2, a transcription factor implicated in rhythmic activity across multiple systems, in ventral posterior medial (VPM) thalamus. Using genetic labeling and optogenetic activation, we show that Shox2 expressing neurons form functional thalamocortical and thalamoreticular projections capable of driving cortical responses. Conditional knockout of Shox2 in VPM alters intrinsic membrane properties, reducing both tonic and burst firing without altering thalamocortical circuit organization or barrel field architecture. These firing deficits are accompanied by impaired whisker-dependent somatomotor performance and a reduction in sleep spindle density in cortical target regions, while overall sleep architecture remains intact. Together, these findings identify Shox2 as a transcriptional regulator required to maintain intrinsic firing modes in VPM thalamocortical neurons, linking a transcription factor to spindle deficits, an emerging neurophysiological biomarker for autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia.

items.title: Music and speech dissociate local temporal irregularity from response strength in human superior temporal cortex
items.blurb: Speech and music engage overlapping auditory cortex. We asked whether they shape the timing of local activity in ways that regional response strength alone leaves unresolved. In intracranial recordings from 30 participants watching a film with alternating music and speech, 1-10-Hz activity in the superior temporal gyrus (STG) had higher sample entropy during music, indicating that similar short patterns were less likely to persist (mean paired difference = 0.02256, FDR q = 0.00753). The contrast persisted in comparisons of adjacent film blocks and was larger relative to surrogate signals matched for amplitude distribution and approximate power spectrum. Speech elicited higher STG high-frequency power in the intracranial subset and stronger bilateral STG BOLD responses in all 30 participants in the separately acquired fMRI recordings. Together, these findings show that the soundtrack category associated with stronger regional responses differs from the one associated with greater local temporal irregularity. The temporal organisation of local activity therefore adds a dimension to how shared auditory cortex responds to natural sounds.

items.title: Local and network-level dynamics of alpha and beta rhythms during visuospatial attention in autism
items.blurb: Visuospatial attention is altered in autism, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Neural oscillatory activity coordinates distributed processes supporting attentional selection and their flexible adjustment to changing environmental demands. Altered oscillatory organization may therefore provide a mechanistic basis for atypical attentional processing in autism. We tested this theory using EEG recordings from 80 autistic and neurotypical children and youth performing a spatial cueing task with valid and invalid cues. We quantified alpha- and beta-band measures of local power and inter-trial phase clustering (ITPC) together with power- and phase-based measures of posterior-frontal long-range connectivity. Across validity conditions, autistic participants showed a more frontal alpha distribution, reduced posterior alpha lateralization and posterior beta ITPC, and higher frontal beta power. Crucially, autistic participants also presented reduced neural adaptation across attentional conditions, reflected in attenuated validity-dependent modulation of alpha power and of posterior-frontal beta connectivity, with elevated beta connectivity particularly in the valid cue condition. This neural pattern was accompanied by greater reaction-time slowing in the invalid compared with the valid cue condition. Within autistic participants, beta dynamics showed nominal associations with restricted and repetitive behaviors that did not survive multiple-comparison correction. Together, these findings suggest that visuospatial attention in autism is characterized by altered local oscillatory organization, combined with reduced modulation of local and distributed dynamics as attentional demands change. Alterations in alpha and beta activity may reflect reduced spatially selective attentional gating alongside greater maintenance of established attentional states.

items.title: HIV-1 Mutational Bias Shapes the Supply of Drug Resistance Mutations
items.blurb: The development of durable HIV-1 therapeutics requires understanding not only which mutations confer resistance, but also how readily those mutations arise. Prior work has characterized the effects of individual mutations on viral fitness and drug or immune escape; however, the contribution of mutational bias to HIV-1 evolutionary pathways remains largely unquantified. Here, we report and provide an interactive HIV-1 Mutation Rate Atlas (MRA), built on a dataset of empirical measurements of single-cycle HIV-1 mutation accumulation in the absence of selection pressure, using error-corrected long-read sequencing. The MRA estimates the mutation rate at every genomic position to each possible nucleotide, enabling evaluation of amino acid mutability across the genome. Using the MRA, we show that mutation rate biases predict HIV-1 drug resistance variant frequencies across patients. These results demonstrate that mutational biases shape HIV-1 evolutionary outcomes, providing a framework for predicting HIV-1 evolution and drug resistance.

items.title: Eukaryotic 45S ribosomal RNA spacers encode an ancient layer of antiviral response
items.blurb: Eukaryotic 45S ribosomal RNA genes produce internal transcribed spacers (ITSs) that are excised and discarded during ribosome biogenesis, with no established function beyond rRNA processing. Here, we uncover an unexpected antiviral role for these seemingly expendable sequences. Comparative genomic analyses reveal extensive, evolutionarily widespread sequence similarities between eukaryotic ITSs and DNA viruses, particularly between vertebrate ITSs and herpesviruses. Across herpesvirus infections, ITS transcripts undergo striking, virus-specific remodeling, largely uncoupled from mature ribosomal RNA production. During herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection, hierarchical Bayesian comparison of competing dynamical models favors active host ITS deployment over passive viral remodeling by odds of 174,000:1. Experimental depletion of ITS2 consistently increases infectious HSV-1 production by approximately 70%, whereas supplementation with synthetic ITS2 RNA generally suppresses viral replication. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized antiviral activity within the 45S rRNA system, challenging the view of ITSs as disposable byproducts of ribosome biogenesis.

items.title: Glioblastoma exhibits bidirectional adaptation to treatment through JARID2-associated developmental plasticity
items.blurb: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits bidirectional transcriptional reprogramming following standard-of-care (SoC) treatment, yet the direction cannot be predicted from primary tumours. Using independent longitudinal bulk and single-cell datasets, we show that this response is captured by a framework, the JARID2 Binding Site (JBS) axis. Tumours and cells can be positioned along this axis according to expression of JBS genes, with responder subtypes defined by movement along the axis from primary to recurrent states. The JBS axis aligns with established GBM ecosystems and their constituent cell populations, and recurrent tumours polarise towards opposite ends. Changes in tumour microenvironment composition strongly influence this polarisation and drive adaptive transcriptional responses more profoundly than chemoradiation alone. Mechanistically, JBS genes are enriched for promoters marked by persistent bivalent chromatin and neurodevelopmental regulatory programmes. These findings suggest that JARID2-associated Polycomb regulation maintains a reservoir of developmental plasticity that enables treatment-driven ecosystem adaptation and represents a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

items.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
items.blurb: Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability. Results: We present ARC-Impute, which regularises cell-to-spot mapping through anchor-residual optimisation, target-guided reference curation and routing, and twin-panel consistency. Across 17 human and mouse datasets spanning spot-based and single-cell technologies, ARC-Impute ranked first for held-out Pearson correlation throughout and exceeded the dataset-specific baseline mean by 47.3% on average. It also achieved the strongest spot-level cell-type composition recovery across three pseudospot benchmarks and retained leading accuracy and consistency under reference and training-gene perturbations. Cross-validated predictions revealed systematic differences in gene imputability. Availability and implementation: Code and workflows at https://github.com/ethanhaan/arc-impute.

items.title: High-Throughput Coded Aperture Raman Imaging with Total Internal Reflection
items.blurb: Spontaneous Raman microscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints of biological tissues, but its low scattering efficiency limits the throughput required for large-area hyperspectral imaging. Here we introduce total internal reflection Raman (TIRR) microscopy, an architecture that exploits repeated internal reflections within a thin sapphire substrate to generate extended evanescent excitation without dividing the incident laser power among independent illumination spots. Combined with programmable Hadamard-coded detection, TIRR recovers spatially resolved Raman spectra with an effective spatial resolution of approximately 3.5 um and a spectral linewidth of approximately 10 cm-1. Hyperspectral imaging of human skin and colon tissues reveals heterogeneous Raman contrast across submillimeter-scale fields of view. Compared with confocal Raman microscopy, TIRR achieves a directly measured 9.0-fold reduction in acquisition time at lower excitation power, corresponding to a 20.1-fold power- and signal-to-noise-normalized acquisition-efficiency advantage. We further demonstrate compressive reconstruction using low-sequency Hadamard patterns, preserving high spectral and spatial fidelity in both the development dataset and an independent tissue specimen. This approach provides an additional nominal 2.1-fold acceleration, suggesting a potential combined normalized throughput enhancement approaching 40-fold. Finally, co-registration with spatial p21 annotations in a human skin section reveals exploratory Raman spectral differences associated with cellular senescence. TIRR thus establishes a programmable approach to accelerated spontaneous Raman imaging while retaining the multidimensional spectral information needed for molecular tissue analysis.

items.title: High-throughput electrochemical transformation expands mass spectrometric reference space for transformation products
items.blurb: Structure annotation of unknown features detected by high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry remains challenging. Spectral libraries provide confident annotation but have limited chemical space coverage. This hampers discovery of natural products and xenobiotics and often necessitates laborious isolation and characterization. We introduce a scalable high-throughput workflow combining online electrochemistry with high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry to expand the empirical spectral reference space for transformation products. This approach enables generating thousands of potential transformation products used for prioritization in non-target datasets. Applying the workflow to 112 chemicals, we generated a suspect spectral library containing 1,341 transformation product entries. Repository-scale matching against public non-target datasets yielded matches for 214 electrochemical transformation products with 70% not annotated by conventional open-access spectral libraries. This workflow provides a source of empirical reference spectra for overlooked transformation products, extends coverage beyond compounds represented in conventional libraries, and supports prioritization of features for structural elucidation, quantification, and bioactivity assessment.

items.title: Functional regeneration of the Rdl-A296S mutation in Anopheles funestus decouples insecticide resistance from genetic background and isolates its life-history costs
items.blurb: Resolving the genetic basis of insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus has been limited both by the historic difficulty of germline transformation in this species and by the confounding genetic and metabolic background present in field populations. The A296S resistance-to-dieldrin (Rdl) mutation provides an informative proof-of-principle case because it has persisted at high frequency in African vector populations long after the withdrawal of dieldrin. Here, we used a marker-less CRISPR/Cas9 homology-directed repair strategy to introduce the A296S mutation in isolation into the insecticide-susceptible FANG strain of An. funestus. WHO tube bioassays were used to quantify resistance across different dieldrin exposure regimes and to assess cross-resistance to other insecticides, while larval development and adult longevity assays were used to evaluate life-history effects. A296S alone was sufficient to confer strong dieldrin resistance. Resistance was context-dependent: homozygous resistance remained robust at higher exposures, whereas heterozygote protection declined with increasing toxic load. No operationally relevant cross-resistance was detected to DDT or pyrethroids. The mutation imposed a modest, recessive delay in larval development, with no detectable reduction in adult longevity and no clear net disadvantage across the life-history traits measured. This study provides the first in vivo functional validation of an insecticide resistance mutation in An. funestus. By isolating A296S on a defined susceptible background, it provides a quantitative baseline for the effect of a single target-site mutation and offers new insight into how stage-specific fitness effects may contribute to the long-term persistence of resistance alleles in natural populations.

items.title: Pyrenophora teres f. teres uses specialized infection structures to facilitate effector-driven promotion of in planta colonization on barley
items.blurb: Pyrenophora teres f. teres is a necrotrophic fungal pathogen that causes net form net blotch (NFNB) of barley. Infection of susceptible barley leaves initially causes dot-like lesions that progress to transverse and longitudinal striations, that form the net-like pattern of necrosis for which the disease was named. While the complex genetic architecture of the P. teres f. teres-barley interaction involves both dominant resistance and susceptibility and quantitative resistance, the in planta infection structures, compatible infection timeline, and the influence of effectors remain poorly defined. This study used fluorescent staining and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) to define infection structures and characterize the compatible infection timeline of P. teres f. teres. Using CLSM in conjunction with image-segmentation machine learning, we generated a clear comparative infection timeline showing how P. teres f. teres isolates harboring zero, one, or two virulence effector alleles infect the barley cultivar Rika. We believe that the effector genes VR1 and VR2 contributed to virulence in a synergistic manner. The effector genes combined presence accelerated the timing and spread of programmed cell death, resulting in significantly greater hyphal volume and visibly more severe macroscopic lesion development. This suggests that P. teres f. teres uses specialized infection structures alongside effectors to maximize fungal colonization and hyphal positioning to optimize nutrient uptake, perpetuating its polycyclic life cycle.

items.title: Multiple Glycans and IFITM Proteins Mediate Human Coronavirus OC43 entry
items.blurb: Human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43 is the most prevalent seasonal coronavirus, causing colds, and occasional severe disease. HCoV-OC43 attachment is reportedly mediated by 9-O acetylated sialic acid (9-O-Ac-Sia); no proteinaceous receptor has been identified. Using genome-wide CRISPR-cas9 screens, we identify several host factors that mediate HCoV-OC43 entry. First, we identify NXPE3, an esterase, as required for HCoV-OC43 attachment and infection, both in vitro and in vivo, and demonstrate a previously unknown role for NXPE3 in 9-O-Ac-Sia synthesis. However, we further show that single residue substitutions in HCoV-OC43 spike, in the S1A domain at the 9-O-Ac-Sia binding site, or two substitutions in the S1B domain, confer 9-O-Ac-Sia independence and a switch to heparan sulfate-dependent entry. Additionally, we find that IFITM1/2/3 proteins act post-attachment to drive HCoV-OC43 virion-cell fusion and entry, irrespective of which attachment mechanism is used. Thus, flexible use of glycan attachment factors enables HCoV-OC43 to access fusion-driving IFITM proteins during entry.

items.title: Deletion of two candidate depolymerases with overlapping genetic effects increases PHA yield in Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1
items.blurb: Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is a microbial carbon-storage polymer with potential as a renewable bioplastic, but intracellular remobilization can limit polymer retention. The metabolically versatile bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1 accumulates PHA during photoheterotrophic growth, yet the enzymes that control PHA turnover in this organism remain incompletely studied. We identified PhaZ2 (Rpal_0568) as a second candidate PHA depolymerase that is evolutionarily and architecturally distinct from the previously annotated PhaZ1 (Rpal_0578). Deleting either PhaZ1 or PhaZ2 alone did not substantially increase PHA content under tested growth conditions, whereas the double mutant accumulated 2.3-fold and 1.7-fold more PHA than wild type under non-nitrogen-fixing and nitrogen-fixing photoheterotrophic conditions, respectively, supporting overlapping roles in PHA turnover. All deletion strains showed longer doubling times but reached final culture densities similar to wild type. The double mutant showed its strongest retention phenotype under severe but growth-permissive nutrient limitation, including 3.7-fold more PHA than wild type at 33% phosphorus availability. A two-stage cultivation strategy that separated biomass formation from nutrient-limited storage raised volumetric PHA titer to 0.180 mg per mL culture in the double mutant, 1.5-fold more than wild type and approximately 3.4-fold higher than single-stage 33% phosphorus limitation and 4.0-fold higher than single-stage 8% nitrogen limitation (cross-experiment comparison), despite lower PHA content per unit biomass. Finally, an LC-MS-calibrated FTIR spectroscopy model predicted PHA content with an R2 of 0.928 (n = 15) and reproduced the major biological trends. These results identify genetically redundant candidate depolymerases as targets for improving PHA retention in TIE-1 and establish a cultivation and screening framework for strain engineering. Importance Persistent pollution from petroleum-based plastics has intensified the need for biodegradable plastics produced from renewable resources. Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is a microbially synthesized bioplastic, but microbial cells can also consume the stored polymer, reducing its net yield. The metabolically versatile, photosynthetic purple non-sulfur bacterium (PNSB) Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1 is a promising production organism because it can photosynthesize, assimilate atmospheric nitrogen, and utilize diverse carbon sources. We show that two candidate PHA depolymerases, PhaZ1 and PhaZ2, likely have overlapping roles in PHA turnover. Removing both candidates increased polymer retention, particularly when nitrogen or phosphorus was limited, and a two-stage cultivation strategy further increased PHA titer to 0.180 mg per mL of culture. We also developed a rapid infrared spectroscopy method to track polymer content across strains and growth conditions. These findings offer complementary genetic, cultivation, and screening strategies for improving microbial bioplastic production and may help advance sustainable alternatives to petroleum-derived plastics.

items.title: Targeting host eIF4A with zotatifin inhibits Bundibugyo virus and other filoviruses
items.blurb: Filoviruses, including Ebola and Marburg viruses, depend on host eIF4A helicase activity for replication. Zotatifin is a first in class, clinical stage eIF4A inhibitor that acts as a molecular glue, stabilizing the interaction between eIF4A and selected polypurine rich RNA sequences, thereby inhibiting RNA unwinding and ribosomal scanning. Here, we identify pronounced polypurine enrichment in the 5'untranslated regions (5'UTRs) of the seven major filoviral protein-coding genes NP, VP35, VP40, GP, VP30, VP24, and L across four virus species, including Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Consistent with these findings, zotatifin inhibits the replication of Ebola, Marburg, Sudan, Tai Forest, and Bundibugyo viruses at low nanomolar concentrations. Zotatifin has been administered to humans in oncology and COVID19 clinical studies. Clinical pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic (PKPD) modeling indicates that exposures resulting in inhibition of BDBV replication are achievable in humans at tolerated doses following subcutaneous administration. Together, these findings support the repurposing of zotatifin as a host directed antiviral candidate against BDBV and other filoviruses, with potential applications in preparedness for future outbreaks.

items.title: Now get out of that! How can the new James Bond film get around 007’s death in No Time to Die?
items.blurb:
Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes

“James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch. No one would believe that one of the world’s most successful film series would come to such an abrupt halt, but no doubt a little reassurance helped.

Nevertheless, the first order of business for scriptwriter Steven Knight and director Denis Villeneuve will be dealing with it: how to revive and re-energise a character at the heart of the action. Speculation on their best way forward has been rife, and previous examples are not hard to find. Sherlock Holmes was killed off by Arthur Conan Doyle by fighting his arch enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls in the story The Final Problem, only to resuscitate him a decade later with The Adventure of the Empty House. Superman is apparently killed at the end of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, but resurrected in Justice League for the fight against Steppenwolf. Arguably the most enduring pop-culture return is Bobby Ewing’s famous shower scene in the TV show Dallas in 1986, which attempted to ensure continuity by suggesting Ewing’s death was his wife’s dream. And even Ian Fleming toyed with killing off Bond, with a climactic poison scene at the end of his 1957 novel From Russia with Love, and leaving him amnesiac and vulnerable to Soviet attack at the finish of You Only Live Twice, the last Bond novel published in Fleming’s lifetime.

items.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
items.blurb:
Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and pathos-drenched, loping forward like an aimless but essential winter morning walk.

While Stillwater captures the spirit of 70s singer-songwriter piano ballads, the rest of Eiger’s forthcoming record is rangier and harder to pin down, touching on traditional folk and loose, minimalist prog. It is undoubtedly the best of his projects to date, and is sure to be one of the year’s breakouts, if recent successes by sharp-tongued songwriters such as Cameron Winter and This Is Lorelei are anything to go by. Shaad D’Souza

items.title: The best recent crime and thrillers – review roundup
items.blurb:
The Taper Man by Nick Harkaway; Watch the Quiet Snow by Mick Herron; Revenge Plot by Stephanie Wrobel; The Voices of the Dead by Nicola Upson; The Bells of Fortune by Leonora Nattrass

The Taper Man by Nick Harkaway (Viking, £22)
The second George Smiley continuation novel from John le Carré’s son Nick Harkaway is set in 1965 and features early iterations of several characters who appear in Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy and Smiley’s People. The cold war is at its height, and British intelligence is keen to protect one of its most important sources, Red Army general Vladimir Vasilev. When a colleague is shot in Helsinki, Smiley discovers a connection to a group of Soviet agents who, through their links to a now defunct spying operation in the US, may jeopardise this key asset. Smiley travels to California to find the “Taper Man”, a sleeper agent whose job is to remain behind when the rest of the network is burned. Meanwhile, leftwing academic Roy Bland goes undercover in Moscow, but things do not go according to plan. Intricately plotted and densely written, The Taper Man takes time to get going, with a fair bit of cold war history and analysis to be digested, but it is a worthy and welcome addition to the le Carré canon.

Watch the Quiet Snow by Mick Herron (Baskerville, £22)
This beautifully presented collection of previously published novellas is the perfect Christmas present for fans of Slow Horses. Two of the stories shed further light on Slough House supremo Jackson Lamb – “a grubby Santa, putting the grot into grotto” – and his shared past with MI5 archivist Molly Doran, while the other three take us into the farther reaches of Herron’s espionage world, where washed-up boozehound John Bachelor works as a “milkman”, looking after retired assets who have “come in from other nations’ colds”. Bachelor’s needs may be simple – shelter, and enough money to pickle himself in peace – but his drunken stumbles into the murky world of double and even triple agents invariably lead to complications and the unwelcome attention of fearsome Service chief Diana Taverner. With Herron’s trademark blend of cynical humour, sinister undercurrents, suspense, irony and pathos, this is a splendid read for a dark night.

items.title: Steps review – Netflix’s Disney-lite Cinderella rework has enough pep in its step
items.blurb:
The plot might be a little overstuffed and the animation style could be a little more distinctive, but this is better than the streamer’s average animated offering

Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but that age-old story you think you know, well, you might not know it at all. It’s a tale as old as Shrek, which was by no means the first film to subvert fairytale expectations, but it was definitely the most influential, and we’re still feeling its impact 25 years later, for better or worse. What if that villain wasn’t actually the villain after all? What if that love interest shouldn’t have been of interest in the first place? What if that damsel in distress was given a bullet-speed fight scene instead of weeping in a tower?

But what might have seemed fresh in 2001, if not quite as fresh for anyone who knew and loved The Princess Bride, has grown a little tiresome ever since. Bucking the conventions has essentially become the convention, and effortful attempts to remix classic storytelling beats have mostly ended up reeking of smugness. Yet they still keep coming (IP is king) and before the inevitable Shrek legacy sequel hits cinemas next summer, Netflix is trying to conjure up that same mix of snark and sentiment with Steps, a Cinderella story but, wait for it, not the Cinderella story you thought you knew …

items.title: ‘My body started consuming itself. I was a millimetre from death’: Andrey Zvyagintsev on Covid, Putin and life in exile

Andrey Zvyagintsev tells the tale of a knight who is riding through a dark forest and sees a stone sign at a fork in the road. The sign says that if he turns left he will lose his horse and if he turns right he will lose his head. So the knight has a dilemma; there are only bad options here. Zvyagintsev smiles and says: “It is a very Russian fairytale.”

Terrible things tend to happen, that’s the way the world works, and a person is defined by how they respond to each challenge. That goes for the knight in the forest and the characters in a film. It probably goes for Zvyagintsev, too, who has lost not his horse but his home and very nearly his life. The Russian director almost died during the Covid-19 pandemic and spent 40 days in an induced coma. He now lives in exile as an enemy of the state. “I’m with the birds,” he says by way of explaining his situation. “Birds have no borders. They’re not thinking about tomorrow.”

items.title: Green Kingdom by Ben Dark review – a luscious natural history of plant life
items.blurb:
A gardener traces the dynasties that dominate the vegetal world in appropriately sumptuous prose

John Ruskin, the Victorian writer and critic, hated the way science insisted on turning his beloved natural world into something smutty. Botanists, he complained, used “microscopic malice” to reduce the spurs, petals and stamens of his favourite flowers to “obscene processes and prurient apparitions”. Others were less squeamish. In 1908, Marie Stopes, the scientist who later became a champion of birth control, spent three days in Japan’s Matsushima Bay in a state of “grand excitement” hunting ginkgo sperms. Oliver Sacks, the neurologist, passed his adolescence at Kew gawping at the cycads’ sexual organs. Reading Ben Dark’s excellent account, it is hard not to conclude that even the most modest plants are living in a state of permanent arousal.

Each of Dark’s chapters tells the story of one plant dynasty, from rootless, seedless pond scum to alpine meadows. Some 97% of all the species that have ever existed are already extinct, but traces of them live on in their descendants, and it is these ancient threads that Dark pursues in this absorbing book. He is a professional gardener, yet his tastes run to the surprisingly sludgy. Orchids and roses have their place in the Green Kingdom, but nothing thrills him more than an evil-looking pond, rich in microscopic nutrients.

items.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
items.blurb:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas

Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”

It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in two versions: a “dark” mix by US producer Tchad Blake and a “bright” version that’s the handiwork of Mike “Spike” Stent, famed for working with everyone from U2 and Madonna to Frank Ocean and Harry Styles.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.blurb:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

items.title: The Guardian view on Britain and Europe: Burnham’s reset cannot be the final destination | Editorial
items.blurb:
It’s welcome news that Labour has reopened doors that the Conservatives slammed shut. But the fundamental dilemma over European integration remains

Andy Burnham on Friday announced a long-awaited deal to ease some of Brexit’s barriers. But EU sources say the agreements, or at least some of them, won’t take effect until Britain has resolved a dispute over its demand for European students to pay the same university tuition fees as British ones. The prime minister had hoped to turn the page on Brexit’s endless haggling. Instead, he was reminded that closer ties come at a price. This does not negate his achievement. The deals ease trade barriers on food, shield British exporters from EU carbon tariffs and let up to 100,000 young people on each side live and work across the Channel for three years. But Mr Burnham cannot claim an unqualified diplomatic victory.

Clearly, such an advance would have been unimaginable under the Conservatives or Reform. The Tories say they will rip up the agreements, though that stance carries the risk of alienating voters lost to the Liberal Democrats in 2024. Nigel Farage admits that Brexit was botched. But he wants greater divergence from, rather than increased closeness to, Europe. Both rightwing parties face a dilemma: how to oppose the better relationship when even Mr Farage acknowledges its benefits?

items.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
items.blurb:
It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers

AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI.

Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital.

Professor Dame Henrietta Moore is founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co-leads The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme

items.title: Don’t blame cyber-attacks for recent outages. The real villain is the US economy | Bruce Schneier
items.blurb:
Our tech infrastructure is riddled with problems. But they’re all downstream of the incentives baked into shareholder capitalism

It’s been a bad week for our computerized infrastructure. We’ve seen outages at Microsoft, the FAA, a handful of banks, United Airlines, an unnamed classified NSA network, and Apple. People should be forgiven for suspecting a coordinated cyber-attack, a common cause, or at least a conspiracy. But there is none.

The incidents are unrelated. They’re not the result of any cyber-attack, coordinated or not. And, even more surprising, they don’t seem to be the result of AI. (We can’t say anything about the NSA; we’ll probably never know the details of that one.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.

items.title: From Bobby Fischer to Magnus Carlsen: 22 of the most famous world chess championship games
items.blurb:
As Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov meet across the board in Geneva, revisit 22 classic games from the world chess championship’s 140-year history

  • Read our World Chess Championship watch guide

The newest chapter in the 140-year history of the world chess championship will be written over the next three weeks in Geneva, where Gukesh Dommaraju of India will defend his title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov. The two 20-year-olds will make history as the youngest ever pairing to contest for the sport’s most coveted title, joining a roll call of great players whose encounters have helped define the game itself.

From the middle of the 16th century, the names of chess players who have been widely regarded as the strongest of their time have been passed down. The earliest of these was the Spanish priest Ruy López de Segura, after whom one of the most popular openings of modern times is named. Others who followed include the Calabrese Gioachino Greco, François-André Danican Philidor, Louis-Charles Mahé de La Bourdonnais, Alexander McDonnell, Howard Staunton, Adolf Anderssen, Mikhail Chigorin and Paul Morphy, each of whom are lionized for their contributions to the development of theory and strategy as well as their dominance over their board during their respective eras.

items.title: Victor Wembanyama has turned his NBA finals humiliation into a revenge tour for the ages
items.blurb:
After a humiliating NBA finals defeat, the 22-year-old has returned with a vengeance – and the Spurs look like contenders again

It wouldn’t be exactly right to say Victor Wembanyama didn’t miss a beat after a disastrous NBA finals in June that left him and his San Antonio Spurs defeated, memed and embarrassed. In the Spurs’ first game this season, against an Oklahoma City Thunder team since decimated by injuries, Wemby went an appalling 1-for-13 from the field. Ten of his 12 points came via free throws. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. It brought to mind an image from the NBA finals a few months earlier: Wemby on the floor after being fouled by the Knicks’ Mitchell Robinson, crowing, “I’m in your head!” The Spurs went on to blow a 29-point lead, lose the game and the finals. Now Wemby seemed too preoccupied with the issues within his own dome to worry about wreaking havoc in anybody else’s.

Game two saw Wembanyama elect to lay the ball up instead of dunking it in the dying seconds of a close tilt with the Houston Rockets, which the springy Amen Thompson blocked spectacularly. Not a great start, and in a league whose narratives calcify long before sample sizes reach an adequate scale, it allowed for whispers that the Spurs were in trouble. But you could say Wembanyama has not missed a beat since then. After beginning the season 0-2, the Spurs are now 13-3, with 12 of those wins coming in a row before a loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton is now the apex sports protester as US athletes stay silent

The Ferrari driver has always used his fame to highlight causes he cares about. Now he stands out as other athletes tone down their rhetoric

Most Formula One drivers might slip away to the beach or the golf course on a week off between races. Lewis Hamilton is not most drivers, though. Instead he went to the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and Gaza. He greeted aid workers in Arabic, toured the checkpoint and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent warehouses in nearby El-Arish, where relief supplies are prepared for distribution. Hamilton made the visit on a day Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza, adding to a death toll that’s climbed above 74,000 since war broke out three years ago. He wore dark glasses and dressed head to toe in black.

“The past three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling,” he wrote on Instagram of his visit, before turning the lens on himself. “I know so many people that feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than watch. I don’t want us to get used to their suffering. I don’t want us to look away.”

items.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season

Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated

The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.

Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing.

After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Simon Burnton

items.title: Ecuador: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 20 November 2026
items.blurb:
Countries: Ecuador, Bolivia (Plurinational State of), El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Mexico, Panama, Peru, United States of America
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

KEY FIGURES

  • 7.9K people displaced in Haiti since mid-October
  • 3.2M people could face crisis-level food insecurity in Guatemala
  • 93K people affected by El Niño-related rains in Ecuador

HAITI: VIOLENCE & DISPLACEMENT

Escalating armed violence across the country is deepening humanitarian needs and restricting access, particularly in densely populated areas of the capital, Port-au-Prince. Since mid-October, violence in Croix-des-Bouquets, on the capital’s outskirts, has displaced about 2,000 people. Nearly 90 per cent are staying with host families and the rest in five informal sites. In late October, attacks in Arcahaie and Cabaret, north-west of the capital, displaced more than 5,900 people. Each new wave puts more strain on stretched host communities. Violence killed an estimated 4,200 people nationwide between January and September, and some 1.5 million people remain displaced. The UN continues to call for the protection of civilians and for safe access to health facilities, schools and other essential services.

CENTRAL AMERICA: FOOD SECURITY

El Niño-related drought is deepening hunger in Central America’s Dry Corridor, where families are running out of food after a failed harvest. An Oxfam assessment of 354 communities in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador found that nearly 8 in 10 maize-producing households lost 75 to 100 per cent of their crop this year. Most now have food reserves for three weeks or less. The drought is also cutting rural incomes: the region’s sugar harvest, a key source of seasonal work, could fall by up to 21 per cent. Projections show about 3.2 million people in Guatemala and 1.8 million in Honduras facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse levels of food insecurity, while up to 249,000 people in El Salvador could face food insecurity.

SOUTH AMERICA: EL NIÑO

El Niño-related rains are worsening along South America’s Pacific coast. In Ecuador, the number of people affected is 93,000 as of 18 November, up from about 65,000 a week earlier, according to the National Secretariat for Risk Management (SNGR). Of these, 36,729 have lost their homes or livelihoods. The rains have led to 16 deaths, damaged more than 25,600 homes, affected over 2,280 schools and 13,000 hectares of crops, and reached all 24 provinces. The National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology (INAMHI) forecasts heavier rain through 21 November. In northern Peru, overflowing streams have cut off several communities in Tumbes, and forecasters warn the Piura River could rise. On 19 November, authorities placed nine Piura and Tumbes provinces under red alert.

REGIONAL: HEALTH ALERTS

Measles and malaria are spreading across the region as gaps in immunization and disease control persist. As of 13 November, PAHO had confirmed 58,213 measles cases and 82 deaths in the Americas this year, more than four times the number for the same period in 2025. Guatemala accounts for most of them, with more than 34,700 cases and 53 deaths. Bolivia, Mexico and the United States have now lost their measles elimination status. Panama has recorded more than 6,700 malaria cases, mainly in the East Panama, Guna Yala and Darién health regions. They include an outbreak of 161 cases in Ancón, an area of the capital, Panama City, where malaria is not endemic. On 16 November, the Ministry of Health declared a national health alert.

items.title: Ecuador: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 20 de noviembre 2026
items.blurb:
Countries: Ecuador, Bolivia (Plurinational State of), El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Mexico, Panama, Peru, United States of America
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

CIFRAS CLAVE

  • 7,9K personas desplazadas en Haití desde mediados de octubre
  • 3,2M personas podrían enfrentar inseguridad alimentaria de nivel Crisis en Guatemala
  • 93K personas afectadas por lluvias asociadas a El Niño en Ecuador

HAITÍ: VIOLENCIA Y DESPLAZAMIENTO

La escalada de violencia armada agrava las necesidades y limita el acceso humanitario, sobre todo en zonas densamente pobladas de la capital, Puerto Príncipe. Desde mediados de octubre, la violencia en Croix-des-Bouquets, en las afueras de la capital, ha desplazado a unas 2.000 personas. Casi el 90% se aloja con familias de acogida y el resto, en cinco sitios informales. A finales de octubre, ataques en Arcahaie y Cabaret, al noroeste de la capital, desplazaron a más de 5.900 personas. Cada nueva ola presiona aún más a comunidades de acogida ya desbordadas. La violencia dejó unas 4.200 víctimas mortales entre enero y septiembre, y 1,5 millones de personas siguen desplazadas en el país. La ONU sigue pidiendo proteger a la población civil y garantizar el acceso seguro a centros de salud, escuelas y otros servicios esenciales.

CENTROAMÉRICA: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA

La sequía asociada a El Niño agrava el hambre en el Corredor Seco centroamericano, donde las familias se quedan sin alimentos tras una mala cosecha. Una evaluación de Oxfam en 354 comunidades de Guatemala, Honduras y El Salvador reveló que casi 8 de cada 10 hogares productores de maíz perdieron del 75% al 100% de su cosecha este año. La mayoría tiene reservas de alimentos para tres semanas o menos. La sequía también reduce los ingresos rurales: la cosecha de caña de azúcar de la región, una fuente clave de empleo temporal, podría caer hasta un 21%. Según las proyecciones, unos 3,2 millones de personas en Guatemala y 1,8 millones en Honduras enfrentarán inseguridad alimentaria en Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) o peor, y hasta 249.000 en El Salvador podrían padecerla.

SURAMÉRICA: EL NIÑO

Las lluvias asociadas a El Niño cobran fuerza en la costa pacífica de Sudamérica. En Ecuador, las personas afectadas sumaban 93.000 al 18 de noviembre, frente a unas 65.000 una semana antes, según la Secretaría Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos (SNGR). De ellas, 36.729 perdieron su vivienda o medios de vida. Las lluvias causaron 16 víctimas mortales, dañaron más de 25.600 viviendas, afectaron más de 2.280 escuelas y 13.000 hectáreas de cultivos, y llegaron a las 24 provincias. El Instituto Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología (INAMHI) prevé lluvias más intensas hasta el 21 de noviembre. En el norte de Perú, el desborde de arroyos aisló a varias comunidades en Tumbes, y los meteorólogos advierten que el río Piura podría crecer. El 19 de noviembre, las autoridades declararon la alerta roja en nueve provincias de Piura y Tumbes

REGIONAL: ALERTAS SANITARIAS

El sarampión y la malaria se propagan en la región ante brechas persistentes en inmunización y control de enfermedades. Al 13 de noviembre, la OPS había confirmado 58.213 casos de sarampión y 82 defunciones en las Américas este año, más del cuádruple que en el mismo periodo de 2025. Guatemala concentra la mayoría, con más de 34.700 casos y 53 defunciones. Bolivia, México y Estados Unidos ya perdieron su estatus de eliminación del sarampión. Panamá registra más de 6.700 casos de malaria, sobre todo en las regiones de salud de Panamá Este, Guna Yala y Darién. Incluyen un brote de 161 casos en Ancón, zona de la capital, Ciudad de Panamá, donde la malaria no es endémica. El 16 de noviembre, el Ministerio de Salud declaró una alerta sanitaria nacional.

Country: Haiti
Sources: CCCM Cluster, Housing, Land, and Property Area of Responsibility, Shelter Cluster, Shelter, Land and Site Coordination Cluster

Cet aperçu mensuel présente la réponse du Cluster Abris, Terre et Coordination des Sites (SLSC) en Haïti : abris et biens non alimentaires (BNA), coordination et gestion des sites (CCCM), et logement, terre et biens (LTB). C'est le premier numéro commun depuis la fusion des clusters Abris/BNA et CCCM.

Faits saillants d'octobre 2026 :

  • Contexte : 1,5 million de personnes déplacées internes (DTM, Round 14), dont 223 821 vivent dans 221 sites actifs.
  • Nouveaux déplacements : quatre alertes ETT suivies en octobre concernent près de 29 000 personnes en Artibonite et dans l'Ouest. Fin octobre, les inondations ont fait 59 420 sinistrés dans l'Ouest et le Grand Sud.
  • Abris et BNA : 54 144 personnes assistées en octobre par 8 partenaires dans 15 communes. Depuis janvier, 345 902 personnes ont été assistées par 20 partenaires dans 44 communes, soit 59 % de la cible du HNRP 2026.
  • Gestion des sites : 128 sites sur 221 (58 %) ont un gestionnaire et abritent 84 % des PDI en site. 93 sites, où vivent 35 756 personnes, restent sans gestionnaire, dont 45 en Artibonite.
  • Redevabilité : 299 plaintes et retours reçus en octobre (4 327 depuis janvier) et 1 039 visites dans les centres de ressources communautaires.
  • Lacunes : aucune activité Abris/BNA rapportée en 2026 dans les Nippes, le Nord et le Nord-Est. L'insécurité limite l'accès à Petite-Rivière de l'Artibonite, Verrettes et Arcahaie.
  • Financement : 27,0 M$ reçus sur 77,6 M$ requis (35 %). 50,5 M$ restent à mobiliser.

items.title: Central African Republic: Situation Report No. 94, as of 17 November 2026
items.blurb:
Country: Central African Republic
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Despite a still volatile context, some humanitarian movements have resumed around Zémio.
  • Infrastructure has been installed in Ouham-Pendé to help prevent agro-pastoral conflicts and reduce tensions between herders and farmers.
  • 3,900 students received school kits in Kaga-Bandoro and M’brès.

GENERAL CONTEXT

Haut-Mbomou Prefecture – South-East

The security situation remains volatile in the Zémio area, despite a relative improvement recently observed along certain roads around the town. In this context, humanitarian actors have gradually resumed some movements and activities in areas affected by movement restrictions that have been in place since September. A limited resumption of civilian movement has also been observed on the main road corridors, while staff from peripheral health facilities have been able to travel to Zémio to replenish medical supplies. No incidents have recently been reported on these routes. A humanitarian organization also conducted movements along the Zémio-Dembia axis to carry out assessments. Given the continuing volatility of the security environment, humanitarian partners are closely monitoring developments and maintaining existing security and risk-management measures.

HUMANITARIAN NEEDS AND RESPONSE

Health

Haute-Kotto Prefecture – Central

On 11 November, the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and its partner International Medical Corps (IMC) concluded their campaign providing comprehensive care for women living with obstetric fistula. A total of 33 patients received specialized treatment in Bria, with an 88 per cent success rate. 15 other patients faced transportation challenges in reaching Bria from Ndele in Bamingui-Bangoran Prefecture. To improve access to services in that area, a second two-week campaign is being conducted in Ndele from 12 to 26 November 2026.

Multi-sector

Vakaga Prefecture – North-East

On 11 November, the NGO COHEB, under a labour-intensive work project implemented through the Emergency Project to Support the Stabilization and Recovery of Refugees and Host Communities in the Lake Chad Basin (PASRRC), distributed cash assistance to 400 beneficiaries, including 150 Sudanese refugees and 250 members of host communities. Through the cash-for-work approach, each beneficiary received 30,000 CFA francs to support livelihoods and meet priority household needs.

  • 3 900 élèves reçoivent des kits scolaires à Kaga-Bandoro et M’brès.

CONTEXTE GÉNÉRAL

Préfecture du Haut-Mbomou – Sud-Est

La situation sécuritaire demeure volatile dans la région de Zémio, malgré une accalmie relative observée récemment sur certains axes routiers autour de la ville. Dans ce contexte, les acteurs humanitaires ont progressivement repris certains déplacements et activités dans les zones affectées par les restrictions de mouvement en vigueur depuis septembre dernier. Une reprise limitée de la circulation des populations civiles a également été observée sur les principaux axes concernés, tandis que le personnel des formations sanitaires périphériques a pu se rendre à Zémio pour s’approvisionner en médicaments. Aucun incident n’a été rapporté récemment sur ces itinéraires. Une organisation humanitaire a par ailleurs effectué des déplacements sur l’axe Zémio-Dembia afin de conduire des évaluations. Compte tenu de la volatilité persistante du contexte sécuritaire, les partenaires humanitaires continuent de suivre étroitement l’évolution de la situation et maintiennent les mesures de gestion des risques et de sécurité en vigueur.

BESOINS ET RÉPONSE HUMANITAIRE

Santé

Préfecture de la Haute-Kotto – Centre

Le 11 novembre 2026, le Fonds des Nations Unies pour la population (UNFPA) et son partenaire International Medical Corps (IMC) ont clôturé leur campagne de prise en charge holistique des femmes vivant avec une fistule obstétricale. Au total, 33 patientes ont bénéficié de soins spécialisés à Bria, avec un taux de réussite de 88 %. 15 autres patientes ont été confrontées à des difficultés de déplacement pour atteindre Bria depuis Ndele dans la préfecture du Bamingui-Bangoran. Afin d’améliorer l’accès à ces services dans cette préfecture, une seconde campagne de deux semaines a lieu à Ndele du 12 au 26 novembre 2026.

Multisectoriel

Préfecture de la Vakaga – Nord-Est

Le 11 novembre 2026, l’ONG COHEB, dans le cadre du projet de Travaux de haute intensité à main d’œuvre (THIMO) mis en œuvre à travers le Programme d’appui d’urgence à la stabilisation et au relèvement des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes dans le bassin du Lac Tchad (PASRRC), a procédé à une distribution monétaire au profit de 400 bénéficiaires, dont 150 réfugiés soudanais et 250 membres des communautés hôtes. A travers l’approche « travail contre rémunération », chaque bénéficiaire a reçu une assistance en espèces de 30 000 FCFA, visant à soutenir les moyens d’existence et à répondre aux besoins prioritaires des ménages vulnérables.

Synopsis (short abstract)

The cereal supply and demand balances included in this report present a subset of data from the FAO/GIEWS Country Cereal Balance System (CCBS) database created and continuously kept up to date by the Global Information and Early Warning System on Food and Agriculture (GIEWS) and Basic Foodstuffs teams of the Markets and Trade Division, with data since 1980. The report contains annual supply and utilization balances for the main cereals produced and consumed for over 220 countries/areas, from which (sub) regional and global aggregates are drawn.

This statistical report contains a subset of cereal country balance sheets (CCBS) data and presents updated cereal supply and demand balances for all sub-Saharan African countries. It complements the information of the FAO/GIEWS Crop Prospects and Food Situation report and is published four times a year with the same schedule.

items.title: World: Food Price Monitoring and Analysis (FPMA) Bulletin #9, 12 November 2026
items.blurb:
Country: World
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Please refer to the attached file.

Synopsis (short abstract)

Global wheat and maize export prices declined in October 2026. Wheat prices fell amid subdued import demand and improving global production prospects, while maize prices declined from their September three‑year high amid seasonal harvest pressure in the United States of America and expectations of ample supplies from South America. Expectations of easing constraints on Black Sea export flows also weighed on wheat prices, although continued logistical disruptions in the region partly offset the downward pressure. By contrast, international rice prices increased, supported by harvest delays in some exporting countries, adverse weather conditions and rising production costs. In most domestic markets monitored by FAO, staple food prices remained relatively elevated in September and October 2026. In parts of East Africa and the Near East, conflict‑related market disruptions, currency depreciation and tight supplies continued to exert upward pressure on prices. In Far East Asia, weather-related production shortfalls and high production costs contributed to the increases in staple food prices, while in Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia, high transport and import costs continued to exert upward pressure on domestic food prices. By contrast, the arrival of new harvests improved market supplies and contributed to seasonal price declines in parts of West Africa and Central and South America. However, strong demand, delayed harvests and unfavourable production prospects continued to drive price increases in some markets. In Southern Africa, ample domestic supplies and continued intra-regional trade helped contain seasonal price increases.

items.title: World: Crop Prospects and Food Situation Triannual Global Report No. 3, November 2026
items.blurb:
Country: World
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Please refer to the attached file.

Synopsis (short abstract)

The triannual Crop Prospects and Food Situation report provides a forward-looking global analysis of cereal production, market trends and acute food security conditions, with a particular attention on low-income food-deficit countries.

FAO estimates that 41 countries/territories require external assistance for food: 31 in Africa, eight in Asia, one in Latin America and the Caribbean, and one in Europe. Persisting conflicts and insecurity remain the primary drivers of the most severe levels of acute food insecurity, while weather shocks associated with the strong El Niño event are worsening conditions in several subregions. Looking ahead, El Niño-related impacts on production are expected to remain severe into 2027 in several subregions, likely aggravating acute food insecurity further.

The report also includes FAO's latest forecast for 2026 cereal production among the Low-Income Food-Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), pegged at 126.5 million tonnes, about 2 percent above both the 2025 level and the five-year average. The increase largely reflects a strong production recovery in Asia, particularly in Near East Asia, while production among African LIFDCs is expected to remain near-average.

items.title: World: WFP presenta su plan para 2027 para asistir a 91 millones de personas necesitadas ante la creciente amenaza de una crisis alimentaria mundial
items.blurb:
Country: World
Source: World Food Programme

ROMA – El Programa Mundial de Alimentos de las Naciones Unidas (WFP) presentó hoy su Perspectiva Global para 2027, en el que detalla sus planes para asistir a 91 millones de personas necesitadas el próximo año, con un costo de poco más de USD 12.000 millones.

Sin embargo, el número de personas a las que WFP prevé brindar asistencia no refleja la magnitud total del hambre en el mundo. Según el Informe Global sobre las Crisis Alimentarias (GRFC), hasta 266 millones de personas enfrentaron hambre aguda en 2025, de las cuales se estima que 39 millones se encontraban en niveles de emergencia o peores.

En medio de este complejo contexto mundial y de las advertencias de que el mundo podría enfrentar su tercera gran crisis alimentaria mundial en seis años, WFP está reforzando su enfoque en medidas de eficiencia que le permitan ampliar su alcance y llegar a las personas más vulnerables. Esto incluye ampliar las iniciativas de acción anticipatoria, como la provisión de seguros y mecanismos de financiación previamente acordados que permitan a las comunidades prepararse mejor antes de que ocurran fenómenos climáticos extremos. WFP también aumentará el trabajo con socios locales y ampliará la asistencia basada en los mercados para aprovechar de manera más eficaz los recursos limitados.

“Para las personas más vulnerables del mundo, escapar del hambre aguda es cada vez más difícil”, afirmó Luke J. Lindberg, Director Ejecutivo de WFP. “Podemos proteger a las personas más vulnerables, pero para lograrlo se necesitarán un compromiso político sostenido, inversión y acción colectiva. Insto a otros a sumarse a nuestro llamado y actuar para garantizar que no haya más hambrunas, que los alimentos no vuelvan a utilizarse como arma y que cesen los ataques contra los trabajadores humanitarios”.

Casi el 72 por ciento de las necesidades de WFP para 2027 están destinadas a la respuesta a crisis, mientras que el 28 por ciento corresponde al fortalecimiento de la resiliencia. Cada contribución a WFP ayuda a salvar vidas hoy y, al mismo tiempo, crea las condiciones para que las comunidades sean más resilientes en el futuro.

# # #

El Panorama Global de WFP para 2027 puede consultarse aquí.

El Programa Mundial de Alimentos de las Naciones Unidas es la organización humanitaria más grande del mundo. Salva vidas en situaciones de emergencia y utiliza la asistencia alimentaria para construir un camino hacia la paz, la estabilidad y la prosperidad para las personas que se recuperan de conflictos, desastres y los efectos de fenómenos meteorológicos extremos.
